root_cause.text: In btmtk_usb_hci_wmt_sync(), the WMT event response SKB data is cast to fixed-size structures (btmtk_hci_wmt_evt and btmtk_hci_wmt_evt_funcc) without validating that the SKB contains enough bytes, allowing a short firmware response to cause out-of-bounds reads.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds skb_pull_data() calls to validate the length before accessing the structures, and the commit message states: "btmtk_usb_hci_wmt_sync() casts the WMT event response SKB data to struct btmtk_hci_wmt_evt (7 bytes) and struct btmtk_hci_wmt_evt_funcc (9 bytes) without first checking that the SKB contains enough data. A short firmware response causes out-of-bounds reads from SKB tailroom."

A short firmware response causes out-of-bounds reads from SKB tailroom."

candidates.rationale: Casts SKB data to a fixed-size structure without checking that the SKB contains enough bytes, enabling OOB read if the response is shorter than sizeof(struct btmtk_hci_wmt_evt).
Dereferences the cast pointer to read whdr.op without verifying there is sufficient data in the SKB, leading to out-of-bounds read on a short response.
Another dereference of wmt_evt->whdr.op in the error print, repeating the OOB read vulnerability without prior size validation.
Second cast from the already potentially undersized wmt_evt pointer to a larger fixed-size structure without checking total SKB length, exacerbating OOB read risk.
Dereferences the second cast pointer to read status, resulting in OOB read if the SKB is shorter than sizeof(struct btmtk_hci_wmt_evt_funcc).
Null check is insufficient; it does not validate the SKB length, so it fails to prevent the subsequent OOB read from a short but non-null SKB.
